title: The Pearl on the Donkey's Neck
summary: Shimon ben Shetach's students buy him a donkey so he won't have to carry heavy loads, and they find a precious pearl tied to its neck. "Now you'll never have to work again!" they cheer, but Shimon ben Shetach wants to return it to its owner. A story about honesty, and about a good name that is worth more than any treasure.
pages: Shimon ben Shetach was one of the greatest sages in Jerusalem, but he was not rich. To earn a living he worked with flax: every day he carried heavy bundles of flax on his back, walked with them from place to place, and came home tired, with an aching back.

His students saw him carrying and huffing, and their hearts ached. "Rabbi," they said, "let us buy you a donkey. The donkey will carry the load, and you will be less tired and can learn more." Shimon ben Shetach agreed and smiled: "Thank you."

The students went to the market. They walked among the stalls until they found an Ishmaelite merchant, who was not Jewish, selling a strong, friendly donkey. They paid and took the donkey. But they didn't notice one little thing tied around its neck…

When they reached their rabbi, one of the students cried out: "Look! There's a pearl tied around the donkey's neck!" A pearl is a precious, shining gem worth lots and lots of money. "Rabbi," they said happily, "now you'll never have to work again!"

But Shimon ben Shetach did not jump for joy. He looked at the pearl and asked just one question: "Does the seller know this pearl was on the donkey?"
"No," said the students. "He surely didn't notice."
"In that case," said Shimon ben Shetach, "we must give it back."

The students were surprised. "But Rabbi, we bought the donkey honestly! And the seller doesn't even know!"
Shimon ben Shetach answered: "What do you think, that I am a wild man? The donkey I bought. The pearl I did not buy."

"I want one thing," he went on. "To hear the merchant say, 'Blessed is the God of the Jews.' That is worth more to me than all the money in the world."
In the Jerusalem Talmud it is written in Aramaic: "Shimon ben Shetach wanted to hear 'Blessed is the God of the Jews' more than all the reward of this world."

Shimon ben Shetach took the pearl and went to the market. He found the merchant and held out the shining stone. "This is yours," he said. "It was on the donkey you sold us." The merchant looked at the pearl, then at Shimon, and again at the pearl. He couldn't believe it.
"Blessed is the God of Shimon ben Shetach!" the merchant cried with excitement. "What an honest man! Who else would return a treasure that nobody even knew about?"

Shimon ben Shetach went home with the donkey and without the pearl, but with a very happy heart. From then on the donkey carried the flax, and he himself had received something more precious than any stone: a good name, and the joy that because of him another person had blessed God.

If you ever find something that isn't yours, a pretty pencil at preschool, a ball in the park or a coin on the sidewalk, remember Shimon ben Shetach. Giving it back isn't always easy, but the feeling afterward shines brighter than any pearl.
